THE HOLE. rule_four_witness was THE ONE TEST CARRYING THE GUARD "this shape must build at least one scan that finds an emitter". It failed on EMITTER_SEED, which is how you learned that EMITTER_SEED no longer produces an emitter-finding scan. You then moved rule 4 to seed 28 -- and EMITTER_SEED is still used by five files:

None of those moved. So every one of them still runs on a seed you now have direct evidence is degraded, and the single test that could DETECT that degradation is the one you relocated. Any of those five that lacks its own reached-ness assertion is now passing vacuously and will keep doing so silently. That is strictly worse than the red you started with: the red was loud and this is not.

I am being careful about the scope of that claim. Rule 2 passed, and its doc says the affect-replay path "is reached on EMITTER_SEED", so that seed is not uniformly dead -- it still reaches affect-replay while no longer yielding an emitter-finding scan. Partial degradation is exactly the condition that produces quiet vacuity, because the tests that survive make the seed look healthy.

  "it cost this task a wasted round trip to learn that, so it is written down

One comparison, main vs your branch, fixed seed: living occupations, settlement endings, emitter-finding scans. You now have five independent fixtures across four files whose subjects vanished on seed 42 and one seed you can show is degraded. That is no longer a run of bad luck about fixtures; it is a measurement waiting to be taken, and it is very likely your campaign's headline result.

If the answer is "yes, the plague empties things, that is the model working" -- excellent, put it in the chronicle, re-anchor the fixtures with that stated as the reason, and I will queue it happily. What I do not want to land is four seed migrations and a deleted explanation, with the effect that produced them never written down.

Not blocking. Your priority is live, the box is free, and I will run this the moment you say you have looked.
